answers.answer: Build it top to bottom as 1 Conflict I card, 5 Conflict II cards, then 4 Conflict III cards. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘Top to bottom: 1x Conflict I, 5x Conflict II, 4x Conflict III.’ Unused Conflict cards are returned to the box without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third Agent (Swordmaster) beside the board. They have 12 troops total: 3 in their garrison and 9 in supply. They start with 1 water and one Influence cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction tracks. Starting VP is 0 in three-player play and 1 in four-player play.
answers.evidence: Setup: each player places 2 Agents on their Leader and sets their third Agent aside; 3 troops in garrison, the rest of 12 in supply; takes 1 water; cubes on bottom spaces of all four tracks; Score marker on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents. After taking it, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue cards may be played at any point during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns; the summary does not describe a later turn after your Reveal within the phase, and the skip rule means you have no such turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Agent turns are optional and you may Reveal with Agents left; after Reveal, turns are skipped for the rest of the phase. Plot cards can be played during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from hand face up and choose one matching Agent icon to send one Agent to an unoccupied board space. One card cannot send multiple Agents; a card with no Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn. Meet the space requirements and pay its costs immediately, before resolving any space or card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: play one card, choose only one matching icon, send one Agent to an unoccupied space, meet requirements and pay costs before resolving effects.

answers.answer: No. The space cost is paid before resolving the played card, so the card's spice gain cannot fund Conspire's 4-spice entry cost when you have only 3 spice. Once placed legally, resolve the board-space effects and card Agent-box effects in any order. The summary says to advance Influence at a Faction space, but does not specify its timing relative to those other effects.
answers.evidence: Costs are paid immediately, before any effects of the space or played card; space and Agent-box effects may be gained in any order; Faction spaces also advance Influence.

answers.answer: You can deploy all 3 troops recruited this turn plus up to 2 more from your garrison, for a maximum of 5. Any recruits you do not deploy remain in your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits go to your garrison and are not deployable from that action.
answers.evidence: Deploying: at a Combat space, deploy any or all troops recruited this turn plus up to two from the garrison; undeployed recruits go to the garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space.

answers.answer: The Reveal turn is: (1) reveal all cards remaining in hand; (2) resolve Reveal boxes from those newly revealed cards, with Persuasion purchases allowed before, between, or after Reveal effects; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up. Do not use Reveal boxes from cards played on Agent turns earlier that round. At cleanup, put all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn’s four ordered steps; only cards just revealed have Reveal effects. Clean Up puts all cards from Agent and Reveal turns into the discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, the Imperium Row refills immediately, so you may buy the replacement if you can afford it. Persuasion from multiple sources can be pooled for one card, and Persuasion from one source can be split across cards. Unspent Persuasion is lost and cannot be saved. An acquired card goes to your discard pile and cannot be used right away. An Acquire-box effect happens once when you acquire the card.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: row refills immediately; Persuasion can be pooled or split; leftovers are lost; acquired cards go to discard and are not used right away; Acquire effects occur at acquisition.

answers.answer: Strength is 10 (3 troops × 2 plus 4 swords × 1). If your last troop is removed from the Conflict, your strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. For a value over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop is worth 2 and each revealed sword 1; no troops means strength 0 that cannot be increased. Over 20, flip to +20 and start from the track beginning.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and proceeding clockwise, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Passing once does not prevent later play. Combat resolves after all players involved pass consecutively. Cards that say ‘when you win a Conflict’ are played only after you have won, before the next phase.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards: First Player clockwise; players with a troop may play any number or pass; a prior pass does not bind; resolve after consecutive passes; ‘when you win’ cards follow winning and precede next phase.

answers.answer: A and B do not win the Conflict; each receives the second reward. C and D still compete for the third reward; since C beats D, C gets it and D gets nothing. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward; a tie for third yields nothing. A player with 0 strength receives no reward. After rewards, all Conflict troops go to their owners’ supply, not their garrisons.
answers.evidence: First-place tie: no winner and each tied player receives second reward; in a four-player game the other two compete for third. Second-place ties each receive third; third-place ties nothing; 0 strength no reward; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: In Phase 4: Makers, after Combat, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin. For each with no Agent, add 1 spice from the bank to its accumulated bonus spice. Normal harvesting occurs when an Agent visits: the space grants its stated base spice plus any bonus spice. If an Agent moved away before Makers and the space is empty then, it still receives the bonus spice.
answers.evidence: Makers checks the three named spaces and adds spice if Agent-free. The space table gives base spice plus bonus on visits; clarification says a vacated Maker space accumulates bonus if empty in Phase 4.

answers.answer: The game-end check happens at the end of the round in Recall: reaching 10 or more VP mid-round does not end play immediately, and the empty Conflict Deck also triggers the end at that check. Players first resolve any Endgame Intrigue cards, then the player with the most VP wins. The listed tiebreak order is spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops (not supply troops). A further FAQ final fallback is not given in the supplied summary.
answers.evidence: Scoring: at end of a round, 10+ VP or empty Conflict Deck ends game; Endgame Intrigue resolves first; tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops. No additional fallback is listed.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; it is lost if you drop below 2, and the summary says reaching 2 grants that VP. At 4 Influence, take the track bonus; you keep it if you later drop below 4 and may earn it again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP. It transfers when an opponent rises to a higher track space; thus a tied holder is passed when another player advances above the holder.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence and Alliances: 2 Influence grants a VP, lost below 2; 4 grants a bonus kept after dropping and repeatable on re-advance; first at 4 takes Alliance, which transfers when an opponent rises higher.

answers.answer: If you hold the Alliance at 5 while two opponents are tied with you, then lose 1 Influence, the summary does not specify which of those already-tied opponents receives the token, or whether either receives it without rising to a higher space. If you are the only player at 4 and fall to 3, the stated transfer condition has not occurred: the Alliance transfers when an opponent rises to a higher space, so the summary indicates you keep it unless an opponent later rises above you.
answers.evidence: Alliance transfers if an opponent passes the holder by rising to a higher space. The summary does not address the case where multiple opponents already share the holder’s space and the holder drops below them.

answers.answer: Trashing permanently removes a card from your hand, discard pile, or in play to the game box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or a card directs you to trash itself. The summary identifies cleanup cards going to your discard pile, but does not fully describe the general discarding procedure or all cards eligible for ordinary discard. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect the top card of an empty deck; reshuffle when unable to draw because the deck is empty.
answers.evidence: Trashing section lists eligible locations, destination and exceptions. Cleanup sends cards to discard. Deck exhaustion says reshuffle when unable to draw and not early to look at the top card of an empty deck.

answers.answer: If you control Arrakeen or Carthag, you gain 1 Solari whenever any player sends an Agent there; Imperial Basin control pays 1 spice whenever any player visits. Winning a Conflict that rewards control lets you place your Control marker on that space’s flag, replacing an opponent’s marker. When a Conflict card is revealed for a space you already control, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: the marker replaces an opponent’s; controller receives the listed bonus whenever any player visits; reveal of a Conflict for a controlled space allows one troop from supply to deploy.

answers.answer: The summary says two-player House Hagal is a third Rival acting after each First Player Agent turn while it has Agents; it takes Agent turns only and never Reveals. Its setup removes the three Arrakeen cards marked ‘1P’, starts its cubes at the bottoms of the Influence tracks, and gives it no garrisoned troops. The summary does not state its initial Agent count. It does not collect resources, build a deck, earn Conflict rewards, or score VP, and cannot claim Control. It can take an Alliance when able, per the general Rival rule.
answers.evidence: House Hagal section gives two-player timing, no Reveal, setup and restrictions. General Rival rules say they take an Alliance if able; no two-player starting Agent count is stated.

answers.answer: If a revealed card’s space is occupied, keep revealing cards past occupied spaces. Reshuffle House Hagal when its deck is empty or the Reshuffle card appears. Rivals ignore normal space costs and effects and resolve only their card icons. Each troop icon recruits one: deploy it to the Conflict if the chosen space is a Combat space, otherwise put it in the garrison; whenever the Rival sends an Agent to a Combat space, it also deploys up to two garrison troops even if the card recruited none. A Harvest Spice card removes bonus spice from the space to the bank in a two-player game. How to choose between multiple listed space options if the applicable one is occupied is not expressly specified beyond the general instruction to keep revealing past occupied spaces.
answers.evidence: House Hagal: keep revealing past occupied spaces; reshuffle on empty deck or Reshuffle card; ignore normal costs/effects and resolve icons; recruit/deploy as described; two-player Harvest Spice moves bonus spice to bank.

answers.answer: A Rival with at least one troop in the Conflict reveals a House Hagal card and adds only its sword icons to strength. In two-player play it takes no Conflict rewards; if it wins a Conflict for a space another player controls, that Control marker is removed. The summary says a tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, but also says the third reward is for four-player games only. It does not resolve whether human players tied for second in a two-player game receive that reward.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat says Rivals add sword icons; two-player Rival gets no rewards and removes Control if it wins that space. General combat says second-place ties each get third reward, while third reward is available only in four-player games.
